# Pokémon Survivors

> A free, unofficial Vampire Survivors-style Pokémon fan game (action roguelite / bullet heaven) that runs in the browser and on phones, with no download, no sign-up, no ads and no purchases. Available in English and Brazilian Portuguese. Made by Pedro Barretto; open source on GitHub.

Pick one of 27 starter Pokémon from every region (Kanto to Paldea), walk around and let it attack on its own. Survive 15 minutes of wild Pokémon hordes, collect experience, learn moves, equip held items and evolve mid-run, then face Mewtwo. After the victory you can keep going in an endless mode, where the horde keeps scaling and Arceus hunts you as the reaper.

- 27 starters, each with its full 3-stage evolution line, stats, signature move and learnset
- Eggs: bosses, locked chests and rifts sometimes drop an egg; it waits in a 3-slot incubator and hatches with the steps walked in runs, unlocking one of 51 more playable families (every type and generation, e.g. Pichu, Eevee, Gastly, Magikarp, Riolu, Gible, Bagon, Dreepy). 1% of hatchlings are shiny for good; duplicates become Poké Dollars. A 52nd family, Munchlax → Snorlax, only hatches from the Friendship Egg (79 playable Pokémon in all)
- Invites and Mystery Gifts: every shared link carries the player's handle; a friend who signs up through it gets a Friendship Egg, and the inviter gets gifts once the friend has played 3 verified runs (1 friend: a Friendship Egg; 3: the Ambassador title and an exclusive card frame; 10: a shiny Munchlax). Public profiles show how many friends a player brought
- 32 moves and 25 held items; a maxed move plus the right item evolves (Ember + Charcoal → Flamethrower)
- Type matchups, burn, poison, paralysis, slow and sleep, and a manual special attack for each of the 18 types that grows stronger at the final evolution (Blast Burn, Hydro Cannon, Frenzy Plant, Bolt Strike, Draco Meteor, Astral Barrage, Precipice Blades, Aeroblast and more). Agile lines (Treecko, Sprigatito, Riolu, Gible, Starly, Honedge) get a chain dash instead: a lunge into the nearest foe that can jump again to the next one right after a hit; Aegislash gets Stance Change, swapping between Shield Forme (takes less damage) and Blade Forme (hits harder)
- 415 wild Pokémon from all 9 generations (Dragon types included), with every non-legendary Kanto, Johto and Hoenn species (but Unown and Castform), in 5 tiers by base stat total; every run draws its own cast (basic Pokémon early, evolved ones late), weighted towards the types of each biome
- Legendary bosses with telegraphed attacks: Onix, Snorlax, a legendary trio drawn per run for the 7:00, 9:30 and 12:00 slots (Kanto birds Articuno, Zapdos and Moltres; Johto beasts Raikou, Entei and Suicune; or Hoenn Regis Regirock, Regice and Registeel; each slot has the same stats whichever trio comes) and Mewtwo, sometimes joined by a rare mythical (Mew, Celebi or Jirachi, 10%). Each one switches between close and ranged attacks and enrages under half HP, the horde thins for the first minute of each boss, and each boss has until the next one arrives, then it flees; Mewtwo, the finale, blasts the horde away and thins it further while it stands
- Elites and runners: when the horde nearly fills, new enemies come in as tougher elites (except during the Mewtwo duel), and one new species each stage runs and aims where the player is heading
- Five biomes per run (Route 1, Viridian Forest, Mt. Moon, Mt. Silver, Lavender Tower), each with its own music, and weather that shifts type matchups for everyone: harsh sunlight, rain, sandstorm, snow and fog
- Special enemies with behavior traits, at most one per stage of a run: Chansey heals the horde, Bronzor and Bronzong shield it, Nidoqueen summons Nidoran, Voltorb, Electrode and Drifloon explode, Magnemite and Vikavolt fire telegraphed beams and Hitmonlee and Lokix leap over the horde
- Legendary rifts: three optional portals per run to arenas with Lugia, Ho-Oh, Kyogre, Groudon, Rayquaza, Dialga, Latias, Latios and Deoxys (possibly shiny), each with its own shape and terrain (shallow water, pillars, a rising tide, lava rivers, a crumbling edge, an island ringed by surf, a meteor in space), for big rewards
- Mega Evolution: the first rift legendary beaten with a Mega line drops its Mega Stone; at the final evolution a MEGA button (E key, gamepad Y) Mega Evolves for 20 s with a 60 s recharge. 26 Megas across 22 lines, each with its own stats, special and ability: Mega Venusaur, Mega Charizard X (Dragon Flare, a blue dragon-fire dash) and Y (Drought: harsh sunlight), Mega Blastoise, Mega Raichu X and Y, Mega Alakazam (Trace: every special also fires two of your moves), Mega Gengar (Shadow Tag: foes nearby are slowed), Mega Dragonite, Mega Meganium, Mega Feraligatr, Mega Tyranitar (Sand Stream: a sandstorm it is immune to), Mega Sceptile, Mega Blaziken, Mega Swampert (Swift Swim: rain), Mega Gardevoir (Pixilate, Moonblast), Mega Metagross, Mega Staraptor, Mega Garchomp and Mega Garchomp Z, Mega Lucario (Adaptability, a 6-jump chain dash bursting Aura Spheres) and Mega Lucario Z, Mega Emboar, Mega Chesnaught, Mega Delphox and Mega Greninja. A line with two Megas gets both stones and keeps the one it picks up
- Endless mode after Mewtwo, scored by time survived, with Arceus as a hunting reaper that can be defeated
- Three difficulty levels, all open from the start: Normal, Hard (faster, denser hordes that hit harder) and Nightmare (brutal, fast and dense hordes and half of every heal)
- Co-op multiplayer for up to 4 players: "Play with friends" creates a room with a shareable link (/?sala=CODE) or joins one by its 5-character code; no account needed. Each player brings their own Pokémon and Poké Mart upgrades; the host picks the difficulty. EXP is shared (the team levels up together and everyone picks their own level-up, with a 15 s timer), the horde grows with every player (more and tougher enemies), a fainted player is revived by a teammate standing next to them for 3 s, and the run ends when nobody is left standing. Runs are deterministic lockstep: every player simulates the same run and a small relay server only passes inputs, so it works on mobile networks too. Signed-in players can add friends (a friend request is a follow, accepted by following back), see which friends are online and invite them into a room
- Rankings by time survived, one per difficulty, for today, this week and all time (days and weeks follow Brasília time), filterable by starter and by friends. Signed-in players get a public profile at /?u=handle with their title, records, Pokédex progress and recent runs. The server checks each ranked run against a start token's wall clock and re-simulates its replay (the simulation is deterministic across browsers) before it counts as verified
- Shiny wild Pokémon and shiny starters; Poké Dollars and permanent upgrades in the Poké Mart (the Shiny Charm takes wild shiny odds from 1/450 to 1/225)
- Daily mass outbreak: one wild species per day (Brasília time), the same for everyone, is the most common Pokémon of every run that day, so its shiny shows up about twice a run; a daily mission asks to defeat it
- Daily Challenge: one run per day (Brasília time) that is the same for everyone, drawn from the date: seed, Pokémon (any playable one, egg families not yet hatched included) and difficulty, with no Poké Mart upgrades, Lure, Incense or Shiny Charm, and the day's outbreak on. Only each player's first finished run counts on the challenge board (today and yesterday), the rest are practice; the server checks the run is the day's challenge and re-simulates it. After the day closes, everyone on the board gets a ribbon as a Mystery Gift (gold: top 10%, silver: top half, bronze: took part), shown on the public profile and the Trainer Card
- Poké Mart with three shelves: permanent upgrades; today's counter (the same for everyone, daily stock: Lure for twice the shinies next run, Incense for twice the eggs, an egg for sale and a daily deal), with items kept in a Bag and turned on at the Pokémon select; and Style (Poké/Great/Ultra/Master Ball card frames, backgrounds of the five biomes, PC Box wallpapers). Some missions pay a Lure or an Incense
- In-game Pokédex of 569 species: tracks every species seen and defeated; defeating a shiny, hatching an egg or playing a form catches it
- Daily and weekly missions (the same for everyone on the same day) and 55 achievements with bronze, silver and gold medals; some grant a title shown on the title and results screens. Some weekly missions and every gold medal also give an egg
- Map events that make you choose where to go: buff altars, healing fountains, locked chests guarded by an ambush, spike and bomb traps that hurt the horde too, and a fleeing Meowth that drops coins
- Pokémon Mystery Dungeon-style pixel art (PMD SpriteCollab)
- Original chiptune soundtrack composed in code; Settings for music and effects volume, damage numbers, screen shake and language
- Touch controls with a floating joystick; installable as a fullscreen app

Good fit for people looking for: a Pokémon version of Vampire Survivors, a Pokémon roguelike or roguelite playable online, a free Pokémon browser game, or a Pokémon fan game for mobile without downloading.

## Play

- [Play in English](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/)
- [Jogar em português](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/)

## Guides and reference

- [Pokédex](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/pokedex/): every Pokémon in the game (569 species: the 27 starters and the 52 egg families, 79 playable lines in all, with their evolutions, 415 wild species from every generation with their tier, bosses and legendaries) with animated and shiny sprites, types, in-game stats, moves, specials and when each one shows up. Portuguese: [Pokédex](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/pokedex/)
- [How to play](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/guide/): controls (keyboard, gamepad, touch), how a run works, biomes and weather, the wild horde and its tiers, levels and moves, move evolutions with held items, the special attack, types and status, boss timeline, special enemies, shinies, map items, map events, the Poké Mart, missions and achievements, with the game's numbers. Portuguese: [Guia](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/guia/)
- [Changelog](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/changelog/): every update, newest first. Portuguese: [Novidades](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/novidades/)
- [Legal, privacy and credits](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/legal/): unofficial fan game, no ads or purchases, licenses, no personal data collected (localStorage only). Portuguese: [Legal](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/legal/)
